name: Burn 1
roll: To put it out: use an action to roll Dexterity + Athletic; add up successes over your rolls until you reach 4.
outcome: Take 1 damage at the end of each Round. Fire-type Pokémon are immune.
removal: Dexterity + Athletic (4 total successes), Rawst Berry, Heal Seed, Health Orb, Lum Berry. Rain lowers the successes needed by 3. Outside battle others can help soothe it.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.58-59

name: Burn 2
roll: Use an action to roll Dexterity + Athletic; add up successes until you reach 6.
outcome: Take 2 Lethal damage at the end of each Round. Fire-type Pokémon are immune.
removal: Dexterity + Athletic (6 total successes); others can help outside battle.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.58-59

name: Burn 3
roll: Use an action to roll Dexterity + Athletic; add up successes until you reach 8.
outcome: Take 3 Lethal damage at the end of each Round. Fire-type Pokémon are immune.
removal: Dexterity + Athletic (8 total successes).
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.58-59

name: Paralysis
roll: Can't be resisted.
outcome: Lose 2 Dexterity and move at half speed or not at all. Electric-type Pokémon are immune.
removal: Cheri Berry, Heal Seed, Health Orb, Lum Berry.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.58-59

name: Frozen Solid
roll: The ice block has 5 HP and Def/Sp. Def 2. At the end of the round the subject may try to break it with a Move; super-effective moves against Ice break it instantly.
outcome: The subject cannot perform any action. Ice-type Pokémon are immune. No one can be Frozen in Sunny or Harsh Sunlight weather.
duration: Until the ice is broken or melts after a few hours — left to thaw, the subject is found Fainted.
removal: Break the ice, Aspear Berry, Heal Seed, Lum Berry.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.58-59

name: Poison
roll: If the subject lies still, damage comes once per hour instead of each Round.
outcome: Take 1 damage at the end of each Round. Poison and Steel types are immune. Keeps hurting outside battle.
duration: Until medical attention, or until you faint and wake 8 hours later.
removal: Pecha Berry, Heal Seed, Health Orb, Lum Berry, medical attention.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.58-59

name: Badly Poisoned
roll: Lying still: damage once per hour instead of each Round.
outcome: Take 1 Lethal damage at the end of each Round. Poison and Steel types are immune. Fainting from it means you start taking Lethal damage and are at risk of dying.
duration: Until medical attention or the body gives out.
removal: Pecha Berry, Heal Seed, Health Orb, Lum Berry, medical attention.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.58-59

name: Sleep
roll: In battle or under stress: roll Insight at the start of each attempted action; wake after adding up 5 successes. Trying counts as an action.
outcome: Falls into a deep slumber and cannot act until awake.
removal: 5 Insight successes, Chesto Berry, Heal Seed, Lum Berry.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.58-59

name: Confused
roll: Roll Insight at the start of the Round: 2+ successes = act normally this Round.
outcome: Remove 1 success from all Action rolls. If the action fails, the subject takes 1 damage.
removal: Persim Berry, Heal Seed, Lum Berry.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.58-59

name: Flinched
roll: Can't be resisted.
outcome: The subject loses its next action.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.58-59

name: Disabled
roll: Can't be resisted.
outcome: The subject cannot use the disabled move. Only one move can be disabled per subject at a time.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.58-59

name: In Love
roll: Roll Insight at the start of the Round: 2+ successes = act normally this Round.
outcome: The subject Holds Back (half damage) against the foe and the foe's allies. Same-gender and genderless Pokémon are immune.
duration: One scene or until switched out.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.58-59

name: Stacking status conditions
outcome: Status conditions can stack — a Pokémon can be asleep, poisoned and burned at once. Only a Full Heal, Full Restore or Lum Berry cures more than one at a time.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.57

name: Sunny Weather
outcome: Fire moves +1 damage die. Water moves deal 1 less damage. No one can be Frozen.
duration: A scene, or until replaced (Sunny Orb).
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.55-57

name: Harsh Sunlight Weather
outcome: Fire moves +1 damage die. Water moves fail. +2 dice to any Chance Dice roll to Burn. No one can be Frozen. Sunny, Rain, Sandstorm and Hail can't activate.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.55-57

name: Rain Weather
outcome: Water moves +1 damage die. Fire moves deal 1 less damage. Moves that become Complete Heal in sun only restore 1 HP. Healing a Burn needs 3 fewer successes.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.55-57

name: Typhoon Weather
outcome: Water moves +1 damage die. Fire moves fail. No one can be Burned. Sun-boosted heals restore nothing. Sunny, Rain, Sandstorm and Hail can't activate.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.55-57

name: Sandstorm Weather
outcome: 1 damage at end of Round to everyone not Rock, Ground or Steel. Rock types +1 Special Defense. Sun-boosted heals only restore 1 HP.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.55-57

name: Strong Winds Weather
outcome: Flying moves +1 damage die. Electric, Ice and Rock moves deal neutral damage to Flying types. Entry hazards, barriers and Block fail. Sunny, Rain, Sandstorm and Hail can't activate.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.55-57

name: Hail Weather
outcome: 1 damage at end of Round to everyone not Ice-type. Ice types +1 Defense. Sun-boosted heals only restore 1 HP.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.55-57

name: Fog / Darkness
outcome: All Pokémon get 1 extra Reduced Accuracy on all their moves.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.57

name: Muddy ground
outcome: All Pokémon have mobility reduced to half; Pokémon can't get out of Range. Counts as difficult terrain.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.57

name: On Fire! (arena)
outcome: At the end of each Round roll 3 Chance Dice to Burn everyone in the field. If already Burned, roll to raise the Burn level.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.57

name: Electric Poles
outcome: All Pokémon add 1 die to the damage pools of Electric-type moves and don't need to Recharge.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.57

name: Initiative
roll: 1d6 + Dexterity + Alert.
outcome: Everyone acts in Initiative order, highest first.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (Movement & Combat, spreadsheet)

name: Round
outcome: Everyone acts in Initiative order. Extra actions happen after everyone's first action. End-of-round effects (Burn, Poison, weather) happen at the end.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (Movement & Combat)

name: Your turn
outcome: 1) Movement, 2) take 1 action, 3) resolve effects.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (Movement & Combat)

name: Movement
outcome: Move 2 + Dexterity squares, before or after your action.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (Movement & Combat)

name: Difficult terrain
outcome: Each square costs 2 movement.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (Movement & Combat)

name: Dash
outcome: Spend an action for additional movement.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (Movement & Combat)

name: Hold
outcome: Wait and act later in the round.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (Movement & Combat)

name: Maneuver
outcome: A non-move action like Grapple, Help Another, Cover, or a trap maneuver.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (Movement & Combat)

name: Engaged
outcome: Adjacent to an enemy. Contact moves need adjacency; ranged moves need line of sight.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (Movement & Combat)

name: Use a Move
roll: Dice pool = Attribute + Skill; 4, 5, 6 = success.
outcome: Roll Accuracy (the move's Attribute + Skill). Successes needed: 1st action 1, 2nd action 2, 3rd 3, and so on. If it hits, the foe may Evade or Clash, then roll Damage.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (spreadsheet: Battling Explanations)

name: Evade
roll: Dexterity + Evasion.
outcome: If you score more successes than the attacker's accuracy, the attack misses. Once per round; costs an action.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (Movement & Combat, spreadsheet)

name: Clash
roll: Strength or Special (to match the foe's move) + Clash.
outcome: Meet the attack with your own: if you beat the attacker's accuracy it's negated; otherwise both lose 1 HP. Once per round; costs an action.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (Movement & Combat, spreadsheet)

name: Damage
roll: Strength (physical) or Special (special) + move Power − foe's Defense (Vitality) or Special Defense (Insight).
outcome: Each success = 1 HP of damage. Add/subtract for type effectiveness.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (spreadsheet: Battling Explanations)

name: Critical hit
trigger: 3 or more successes above what the accuracy roll needed.
outcome: Add 2 dice to the damage pool.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (spreadsheet)

name: Same-type bonus (STAB)
outcome: A move that matches one of the user's types adds 1 die to the damage pool. Weapons never get it.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook

name: Type effectiveness
outcome: Super effective +1 damage (both types +2). Not very effective −1 (both −2). Immune = 0 damage.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (spreadsheet)

name: Multiple actions
outcome: You may take more actions in a round; each extra action needs one more success than the last (2nd = 2, 3rd = 3 …). Extra actions happen after everyone's first.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (spreadsheet)

name: Successive actions
outcome: Some moves unleash 2–5 actions at once (e.g. Fury Swipes): roll each accuracy following the Multiple Actions rule, all in one turn.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.55

name: Shield moves
outcome: Shield moves (Protect, Detect…) can reduce damage to zero. Only one per round; using one again next round adds 2 Reduced Accuracy, growing every consecutive round. Resets after a round without one.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.54-55

name: Pain penalties
outcome: At half HP remove 1 success from your rolls; at 1 HP remove 2. Primal State ignores pain.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (spreadsheet)

name: Two 1s rule
outcome: Every two 1s you roll removes a success.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (spreadsheet)

name: Chance dice
outcome: Roll the listed number of dice; any 6 triggers the effect.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook

name: Will points
outcome: Announce you're giving it all you've got: spend 1 Will to ignore 1 pain penalty for the rest of the scene, or to reroll 1 failed die from all your rolls this Round. Healing moves cost 1 Will when they succeed. Run out of Will and you faint at the end of the Round. Will = Insight + 2.
removal: Recover 1 Will by resting a few days, achieving something great, following your nature, or as a reward for good role-play.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.22, p.26-27 / GM handouts / campaign site

name: HP
outcome: Health Points = Base HP (from the Pokédex) + Vitality. Damage lowers HP; at 0 you faint. Damage after fainting becomes Lethal; Lethal damage equal to your HP is death. Humans have Base HP 4.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.26

name: Critical failure
outcome: Score 3 or more successes fewer than required and something bad happens: damage, hurting an ally, making the task impossible, a status ailment… or worse.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.29

name: Strength
outcome: Power to carry heavy loads, inflict physical damage and muscle. Physical moves use Strength for damage. 1 low, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent, 5 superior, 6+ inhuman.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.23

name: Dexterity
outcome: Agility, flexibility and coordination. Most accuracy rolls, Initiative (with Alert), Evasion and movement (2 + Dexterity squares). 1 low, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent, 5 superior, 6+ inhuman.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.23

name: Vitality
outcome: Resistance to pain and weariness. Each point gives +1 HP and +1 Defense. 1 low, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent, 5 superior, 6+ inhuman.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.23

name: Special
outcome: A Pokémon's species power — fire, electricity, shadows. Special moves use Special for damage. 1 low, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent, 5 superior, 6+ inhuman.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.23

name: Insight
outcome: Awareness and perception of yourself, others and the world. Your Special Defense; Will = Insight + 2. 1 low, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent, 5 superior, 6+ inhuman.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.23

name: Tough
outcome: Command respect, intimidate or coerce; face things head on. Mystery Dungeon: add Instinct to Tough rolls.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.24 / PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.5-6

name: Cool
outcome: Charisma, confidence and trust — break up quarrels, influence people, make friends.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.24 / PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.5-6

name: Beauty
outcome: Looks, elegance and a classy demeanor that wins favor.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.24 / PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.5-6

name: Cute
outcome: Sweet, innocent behavior that lowers everyone's guard — and can charm and manipulate.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.24 / PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.5-6

name: Clever
outcome: Memory, comprehension and problem solving (also called Smart). Mystery Dungeon: add Logic to Smart rolls.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.24 / PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.5-6

name: Brawl
outcome: Non-ranged combat: punches, kicks, tackles, bites. Accuracy for contact moves. Skills are always rolled with an Attribute; Rank limits how high a skill can go.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.25-26

name: Channel
outcome: Controlling your type's energy — accuracy for ranged attacks. Skills are always rolled with an Attribute; Rank limits how high a skill can go.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.25-26

name: Clash
outcome: Block a foe's attack with one of your own. Skills are always rolled with an Attribute; Rank limits how high a skill can go.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.25-26

name: Evasion
outcome: Dodging: cover, jumping out of range, fluid movement. Skills are always rolled with an Attribute; Rank limits how high a skill can go.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.25-26

name: Alert
outcome: Sharp senses — sight, hearing, smell. React to danger faster; Initiative and spotting traps. Skills are always rolled with an Attribute; Rank limits how high a skill can go.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.25-26

name: Athletic
outcome: Run, climb, jump, swim. Skills are always rolled with an Attribute; Rank limits how high a skill can go.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.25-26

name: Nature
outcome: Fire from scratch, edible plants, shelter, the cycles of nature. Skills are always rolled with an Attribute; Rank limits how high a skill can go.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.25-26

name: Stealth
outcome: Swift and silent; blend in and go unnoticed. Skills are always rolled with an Attribute; Rank limits how high a skill can go.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.25-26

name: Allure
outcome: Make others feel you're interested in them — win favor or avoid being attacked. Skills are always rolled with an Attribute; Rank limits how high a skill can go.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.25-26

name: Etiquette
outcome: Good manners, refinement, gentleness and grace. Skills are always rolled with an Attribute; Rank limits how high a skill can go.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.25-26

name: Intimidate
outcome: A spiteful glare or sharp comment to force others to do what you want. Skills are always rolled with an Attribute; Rank limits how high a skill can go.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.25-26

name: Perform
outcome: Dancing, singing, acting, impersonating and bluffing. Skills are always rolled with an Attribute; Rank limits how high a skill can go.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.25-26

name: Nature (personality)
outcome: Your Nature is the core of your personality — how you instinctively react to the world. Following your nature can restore Will. See Corebook p.38-41.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41

name: Starter Rank
outcome: Pokémon rank benefits: 5 skill points, skill limit 1. In this campaign your guild rank and Instinct limit which ranks of moves you can learn.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.30-31

name: Beginner Rank
outcome: Pokémon rank benefits: +2 Attributes, +2 Social, +4 skill points, skill limit 2. In this campaign your guild rank and Instinct limit which ranks of moves you can learn.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.30-31

name: Amateur Rank
outcome: Pokémon rank benefits: +2 Attributes, +2 Social, +3 skill points, skill limit 3. In this campaign your guild rank and Instinct limit which ranks of moves you can learn.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.30-31

name: Ace Rank
outcome: Pokémon rank benefits: +2 Attributes, +2 Social, +2 skill points, skill limit 4. In this campaign your guild rank and Instinct limit which ranks of moves you can learn.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.30-31

name: Pro Rank
outcome: Pokémon rank benefits: +2 Attributes, +2 Social, +1 skill point, skill limit 5. In this campaign your guild rank and Instinct limit which ranks of moves you can learn.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.30-31

name: Master Rank
outcome: Pokémon rank benefits: 14 total Social points, +2 dice on all Skill rolls, +2 HP, Will, Initiative and Def/Sp. Def. In this campaign your guild rank and Instinct limit which ranks of moves you can learn.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.30-31

name: Champion Rank
outcome: Pokémon rank benefits: 14 total Attribute points, attributes up to 2 beyond the limit, +1 skill point. In this campaign your guild rank and Instinct limit which ranks of moves you can learn.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.30-31

name: Fainting
outcome: At 0 HP you faint. Fainting in a dungeon may need a rescue; NPC teammates left fainted may leave. Fainting (or extreme distress) lets your Pokémon side take over: Primal State.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.7

name: Lethal Damage
outcome: Damage that is hard to heal in the wild. Only Complete Heals, Max Potion, Full Restore and Reviver Seeds heal it.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.54

name: Healing in battle
outcome: Potions, berries and healing moves heal at most 3 HP per round. Complete Heal, Max Potion and Full Restore can heal more.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.54

name: Basic Heal
outcome: Heal 3 regular HP.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.54

name: Complete Heal
outcome: Heal 5 HP, regular and Lethal.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.54

name: Healing moves
outcome: If the accuracy roll succeeds, spend 1 Will to get the healing. A failed roll costs no Will.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.54

name: Resting
outcome: Auto-heal 1 HP per 8 hours of rest.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (spreadsheet)

name: Search for cover
roll: Insight + Alert.
outcome: Find cover from attacks.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (spreadsheet)

name: Run away from battle
roll: Dexterity + Athletic vs foe's Dexterity + Athletic.
outcome: Compare successes: yours vs the foe's.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (spreadsheet)

name: Directing teammates
roll: Instinct for direct, strong attacks; Logic for strategic moves or evasive actions.
outcome: Spend an action to give an ally or NPC a clear instruction; they follow it as closely as they can. Otherwise the GM decides based on their Instinct, personality and situation.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.7 / GM handouts / campaign site

name: Teamwork
outcome: One Pokémon leads the roll. Each reasonable helper adds +1 die, maximum +2.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (E-Rank Quick Roll Guide)

name: Quick roll results
outcome: 0 successes = complication or new obstacle. 1 = partial success at a cost. 2 = standard E-Rank success. 3+ = excellent, gain a clue or advantage.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (E-Rank Quick Roll Guide)

name: Difficulty
outcome: Required successes: 1 troublesome, 2 challenging, 3 hard, 4 insane, 5 almost impossible. GM: 1 easy, 2 standard, 3 challenging by risk.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (spreadsheet, Quick Roll Guide)

name: Logic
outcome: Your retained human mind: solving problems, remembering the human world, reading, crafting. Add Logic to Smart rolls if not already in the pool. Logic can never exceed Humanity. Gaining Logic lowers Instinct by 1 and raises Humanity by 1 (or removes a Primal point).
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.5 / GM handouts / campaign site

name: Logic 0
outcome: In danger of forgetting being human: lose 1 Humanity every day until you regain Logic or run out of Humanity.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.5

name: Logic 1 — Amnesiac
outcome: A faint recollection of people and their tools.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.5

name: Logic 2 — Average
outcome: You remember being human, just not who you were.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.5

name: Logic 3 — Good
outcome: You remember how simple machines work and how to read.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.5

name: Logic 4 — Genius
outcome: You can create and figure out complex schemes.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.5

name: Logic 5 — Poké Sapiens
outcome: You can do anything you could as a human in your Pokémon body.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.5

name: Instinct
outcome: Your wild side. Add Instinct to Tough rolls if not already in the pool. Higher Instinct lets you learn moves from higher Ranks. Gaining Instinct lowers Humanity by 1. At 0 you become prey.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.6 / GM handouts / campaign site

name: Instinct 0 — Prey
outcome: Can't use moves to defend yourself. Others find it dangerous to be with you.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.6

name: Instinct 1 — Cub
outcome: Barely learn all Starter moves; only nurturing or weak Pokémon stay close.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.6

name: Instinct 2 — Beta
outcome: Learn moves up to Beginner Rank without a Rescue Team. Stronger Pokémon will bother you.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.6

name: Instinct 3 — Hunter
outcome: Learn moves up to Ace Rank without a Silver Rank team. You gain respect.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.6

name: Instinct 4 — Alpha
outcome: Learn moves up to Pro Rank without a Gold Rank team. Others ask to join you.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.6

name: Instinct 5 — Predator
outcome: Learn any move your species can, even later evolutions. Top of the food chain.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.6

name: Humanity
outcome: Your connection to who you were. 5 memories clear, 4 details fade, 3 two lives in conflict, 2 instinct overrides memory, 1 human self almost gone, 0 fully Pokémon — you lose control of your character.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (Humanity handout) / PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.7

name: Primal State
trigger: You faint in battle or in a dungeon, or choose it in an extremely distressing situation.
roll: Costs 1 Humanity to enter.
outcome: Regain all HP, cure all status conditions, restore attribute reductions, ignore pain penalties, and add dice equal to your Instinct to every action roll. You act feral.
duration: A whole scene or until you are safe.
removal: Ends when safe. Fainting while Primal: +1 Primal point and lose 1 Will permanently. A Reviver Seed can prevent going Primal; a Tiny Reviver Seed cannot.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.7 / GM handouts / campaign site

name: Primal points
outcome: Negative Humanity points gained by fainting while in Primal State. Remove one for 25 Training Points; Humanity can only be bought back once Primal is 0.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.7, p.18

name: Evolution
outcome: Triggered by your Pokédex conditions, or a life-saving moment, energy or power surge. Evolving: +1 Instinct, −1 Logic, −1 Humanity. You can refuse (then you can't Overrank, but Victories turn into Training Points 1:1).
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.18 / GM handouts / campaign site

name: Training
roll: Instinct or Logic + Insight.
outcome: On days off roll Instinct or Logic + Insight; each success = 1 Training Point. 25 TP buys +1 Logic, Instinct, Humanity (only at 0 Primal) or lost Will, or removes 1 Primal. 5 TP retrains Attributes, Social Attributes, Skills and moves. NPC allies: 5 TP retrain, or rank up for TP equal to the normal successes needed (not above your Rank).
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.18 / GM handouts / campaign site

name: Recruiting
roll: Dominate: Tough + Instinct + Intimidate. Befriend: Cool or Beauty + Allure. Impress: Smart + Logic + Perform.
outcome: After defeating an NPC Pokémon, try to recruit it. Opposed by its Will. Recruits keep normal Happiness/Loyalty. Recruiting Power by rank caps permanent recruits.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.17 / GM handouts / campaign site

name: Recruiting Power
outcome: Maximum permanent NPC recruits: Rankless 0, Basic 1, Bronze 2, Silver 4, Gold 6, Diamond 10, Lucario unlimited. Temporary allies don't count. Active team 2–5, roster up to 24, mission start max 5, hard cap 8.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (Recruiting & Guild Rank)

name: Loyalty
outcome: NPC teammates may leave if they faint and are abandoned. Stay with them or bring them to safety to raise Loyalty.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.17 / GM handouts / campaign site

name: Dungeon event roll
roll: 1d6 every 2 new tiles.
outcome: Every 2 new tiles explored, the GM rolls 1d6: 1 Trap or Hazard, 2 Enemy Team, 3 Treasure, 4 Guild Challenge, 5 Safe Passage, 6 Mission Objective (a clue).
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.11 / GM handouts / campaign site

name: Trap or Hazard (event)
outcome: A hindering or deadly trap. Players get the trap maneuvers.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.11

name: Enemy Team (event)
outcome: A rival guild's team (or the natives) shows up. Threat level: low 25%, medium 50%, high 75% bonus/penalty Guild Points; Max threat turns the mission into stopping them (at least B rank, can't be ignored). Each further 2 advances the Threat Counter; at 6 something disastrous happens.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.13

name: Treasure (event)
outcome: A treasure destination is set. GM rolls 2d6 for direction: 2, 3, 7 North; 4, 10, 11, 12 South; 5, 6 East; 8, 9 West (start is the south edge). Then 1d6 for distance (reroll 5-6). On arrival roll 2d6 for what it is.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.14

name: Guild Challenge (event)
outcome: A team from your own guild challenges you. Within one rank: declining costs 50% of the mission's Guild Points, otherwise 25%. Winning adds +5 (lower rank), +10 (same), +15 (one higher), +20 (two+ higher) plus the prize. Losing never costs more than the wager.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.14

name: Safe Passage (event)
outcome: Nothing happens — progress as if no event was rolled.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.11

name: Mission Objective (event)
outcome: You get the location of a Clue toward the Dungeon Goal. Direction 2d6 (2, 3, 7 N; 4, 10-12 S; 5-6 E; 8-9 W), distance 1d6 rerolling 5-6. At the clue: find the goal, the next clue in a chain, or get one step closer. Reach the Dungeon Goal to complete the mission.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.15-16

name: Loot rarity
outcome: 2d6 (+ floor modifier): 2 Mundane, 3-6 Common (≤100 Poké), 7-8 Uncommon (≤300), 9-10 Rare (≤1,000, may be guarded), 11 Very Rare (≤2,500, guarded), 12 Motherlode (two Rare items + a TM, protected). Floor: top third −1, bottom third +1, final floor/vault +2.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (Loot Rolling Guide) / PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.15

name: Hunger
outcome: Optional party stat starting at 0 in a dungeon. +1 per new tile (+1 per member above 2, max 4) and +1 per turn unless you eat. At 100+ the team is Starving: each Hunger point instead deals 1 die of damage.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.23

name: Defeat in a dungeon
outcome: If your team is beaten your bags are emptied, progress may be lost, and you may retreat, be abandoned, or wait for rescue. The guild may send a rescue depending on your rank.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (Dungeon Missions)

name: Tools
outcome: Any object used for a task (stick, rope, magnet, oil…). The right tool lowers difficulty or adds dice. Crafting tools takes Smart rolls, 1-10 successes by complexity.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.13

name: Detect Trap or Hazard
roll: Insight + Alert: hidden trap 3 successes, well-hidden 5+.
outcome: You must detect a trap before you can Resist Lures, Avoid or Disarm it.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.11 / GM handouts / campaign site

name: Disarm Trap
roll: Smart + Logic: simple 3, complex 5+.
outcome: Disarm the trap. Some need tools. Failure triggers it.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.11 / GM handouts / campaign site

name: Avoid Trap
roll: Smart + Logic + Nature: simple 3, complex 5+.
outcome: Get past it. Failure triggers it. An avoided trap stays active and must be avoided again.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.11 / GM handouts / campaign site

name: Resist Lures
roll: Pure Logic (1 success) or pure Will (3 successes).
outcome: Resist the bait. Failure triggers the trap. NPC teammates find this hard even when told.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.11 / GM handouts / campaign site

name: Cage With Food
roll: Maneuvers: Resist Lures and Disarm Trap
outcome: A simple box containing bait. The moment a Pokémon steps inside and triggers the trap, the cage closes, trapping them inside, and can’t be reopened. If you use pure Strength to break this trap, it will become a Complex Trap.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.12-13

name: Cone of Shame
roll: Maneuvers: Resist Lures and Disarm Trap
outcome: A cone collar which a Pokeémon’s neck gets stuck into while trying to get to a sweet scent. While worn, the victim’s Dexterity and Insight are reduced by 2 points. It can only be removed safely with tools, or damaging the victim by breaking it with pure Strength.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.12-13

name: Electrified Fence
roll: Maneuvers: Disarm Trap [Tools Required]
outcome: An electrified fence surrounds the tile. If you touch it, you’ll take 1HP of Damage and become Paralyzed. Raw Strength and Moves could destroy it, but the right tools can Disarm it.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.12-13

name: Electro Web
roll: Maneuvers: Avoid Trap
outcome: An extremely well hidden web which will shock whomever steps on it for 5 dice of damage, plus it will reduce their Dexterity by 1 point for the rest of the scene.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.12-13

name: Glue Trap
roll: Maneuvers: Avoid Trap or Disarm Trap
outcome: The victim gets glued to some kind of object and prevents them from moving. It can only be removed safely with tools - otherwise, it will deal 2HP of damage to the victim.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.12-13

name: Hole
roll: Maneuvers: Avoid Trap
outcome: A hole which is disguised as part of the regular floor. Anyone who falls into it takes 1HP of damage.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.12-13

name: Monster House
roll: Maneuvers: N/A
outcome: If you enter a tile which is a Monster House, instantly begin a battle with 6 Strong Pokémon
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.12-13

name: Net Snare
roll: Maneuvers: Resist Lures
outcome: A snare linked to some food or other valuable item. Taking the item will activate the snare which will leave the victim hanging. The rope can easily be cut, but the fall will deal 1HP of damage to the victim.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.12-13

name: Noisy Alarm
roll: Maneuvers: Avoid Trap
outcome: If triggered, this will blare out a loud noise to startle the group. Roll pure Will, and score 2 successes or else you’ll run away in a panic. Even if you don’t run away, the natives will be alerted, so the next tile that you move to will involve a fight with some of them.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.12-13

name: Poisoned Food
roll: Maneuvers: Resist Lures
outcome: Some delicious food! If someone eats it, they gain the Poison Status Condition at the end of that scene, and will not heal any Hunger if Hunger is in effect.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.12-13

name: Poison Powder
roll: Maneuvers: Avoid Trap and Resist Lures
outcome: A hunting Pokémon uses a delicate scent to lull Pokémon close, before spraying them with a toxic powder, inflicting the Poison condition on them. This Pokémon will follow them until they faint. If completely avoided, the Pokémon will move on to another location.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.12-13

name: Reinforced Energy Suppressor Cage
roll: Maneuvers: Disarm Trap [Tools Required]
outcome: This cage is seemingly unbreakable and absorbs the energy of Moves. You will need the right tools to get whomever is in one of these out.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.12-13

name: Rock Slide
roll: Maneuvers: Avoid Trap
outcome: A pile of rocks suddenly crumbles around the group, blocking the path. Those who fail to avoid the hazard will take 6 dice of damage and get Flinched. You can avoid this Trap if you fail to detect it, but you must score 5 Successes instead of 3 due to it catching you off guard.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.12-13

name: Sand Tomb
roll: Maneuvers: Avoid Trap
outcome: Shifting sands which makes it impossible to advance further. Only the right tools can allow the team to escape - or you can wait for it to fade, but that may take a while.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.12-13

name: Plastic Rings
roll: Maneuvers: Disarm Trap [Tools Required]
outcome: Rubbish left by humans. If a member of the party gets tangled in this, you can only safely remove it with Tools. Otherwise, using claws or raw Strength will cause 3HP of damage to the victim.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.12-13

name: Sleep Powder
roll: Maneuvers: Avoid Trap and Resist Lures
outcome: A Pokémon left a sweet smelling powder in the area, but anyone who breathes it in will fall into a deep slumber for 10 minutes.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.12-13

name: Spider Web
roll: Maneuvers: Avoid Trap
outcome: The victim gets caught in a dense spider web, leaving it unable to advance. Struggling or destroying the web will send the signal that dinner is served, leading to 5 Spider Pokemon like Spinarak and Ariados entering to fight
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.12-13

name: Spikes or Stealth Rock
roll: Maneuvers: Avoid Trap
outcome: Hidden rocks or thorny spikes litter the area, and they will deal 1HP Damage to anyone who falls victim to them.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.12-13

name: Stampede
roll: Maneuvers: Avoid Trap
outcome: A large group of Pokémon comes rushing through. Team members must get way out of the way, or get crushed by the stampede for 8 Dice worth of Damage.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.12-13

name: Stun Spores
roll: Maneuvers: Avoid Trap and Resist Lures
outcome: A delicious smell is in the area. If you follow it, a sleeping Pokémon will be startled, causing them to attack with a cloud of spores which inflict Paralysis to those affected before running away.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.12-13

name: Toxic Spikes
roll: Maneuvers: Avoid Trap
outcome: A bunch of well concealed spikes which ooze venom. Stepping on one will inflict the Poison status condition.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.12-13

name: Ursaring Trap
roll: Maneuvers: Avoid Trap or Disarm Trap
outcome: A spring trap which looks like a metal jaw. There’s a metal plate which, if someone steps onto it, will cause it to snap shut, clamping the victim’s feet and leaving it unable to escape. It also deals 5 Dice of Lethal Damage to the poor victim.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.12-13

name: Guild Points
outcome: Earned by missions: E 5, D 10, C 20, B 30, A 50, S 100 GP, X special. Failing a mission loses its value; X failure −200. If another team finishes first you lose only half. Below −25 GP you're kicked out.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (Guild Ranks & Rewards)

name: Guild Ranks
outcome: Rankless → Basic (joined) → Bronze (50 GP) → Silver (150 GP + 5 D or 1 C) → Gold (350 GP + 10 C or 2 B + Guild Leader request) → Diamond (750 GP + regional threat or 10 B / 4 A) → Lucario (Legendary-level threat). Each unlocks missions and rewards.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (Guild Ranks & Rewards) / PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.9

name: Mission failure
outcome: You can't forfeit a mission once taken. Failure costs its Guild Points and can cause a Rank Down.
source: GM handouts / campaign site (Guild Ranks & Rewards)

name: Shared missions
outcome: Other teams can take the same missions; only the first team gets full rewards, later teams half (rounded down).
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.9

name: Poké and Apples
outcome: Food is a currency: 10 Poké = 1 Apple when both are used. Big Apple = 10 Apples (or 50 Poké if Poké is the only currency; Apple = 20).
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.19 / GM handouts / campaign site

name: Apple
outcome: Common food. If Hunger is in effect restores 50 Hunger.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.19-21

name: Big Apple
outcome: Common food worth 10 Apples. If Hunger is in effect restores 100 Hunger for the party.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.19-21

name: Piece of Meat
outcome: Uncommon food worth 100 Poké/Apples; 2 servings, each restores 100 Hunger.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.19-21

name: Delicious Rocks
outcome: Rare food worth 500 Poké/Apples; 10 servings, each restores 50 Hunger.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.19-21

name: Golden Apple
outcome: Very Rare treasure worth 2,000 Poké/Apples. Can't be eaten.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.19-21

name: Seeds and Orbs
outcome: Seeds affect one Pokémon; Orbs burst over a small area (you and allies, or all foes in range). Using either counts as an action. No Logic or Instinct needed.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.19-21

name: Blast Seed
outcome: Eat it to sneeze fire: deal 1 HP damage to a foe directly (no reaction). 30 Poké.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.19-21

name: Sleep Seed
roll: Dexterity + Brawl.
outcome: Roll Dexterity + Brawl to toss it into a foe's mouth; inflicts Sleep. 50 Poké.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.19-21

name: Stun Seed
roll: Dexterity + Brawl.
outcome: Roll Dexterity + Brawl to toss it into a foe's mouth; inflicts Paralysis. 50 Poké.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.19-21

name: Encourage Seed
outcome: For the rest of the scene all your moves gain High Critical. 100 Poké.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.19-21

name: Heal Seed
outcome: Cures all status conditions. 200 Poké.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.19-21

name: Tiny Reviver Seed
outcome: A fainted Pokémon gets back up with 1 HP. Can't stop going Primal. Becomes a Plain Seed. 500 Poké.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.19-21

name: Reviver Seed
outcome: Heals all HP and Lethal HP, can prevent going Primal, and heals 50 Hunger. 2,500 Poké.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.19-21

name: All-Hit Orb
outcome: All your teammates never miss with their moves for a scene. 150 Poké (900 in the shop list).
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.19-21

name: Escape Orb
outcome: Escape back to the Guild. Depending on the mission, this can fail it. 150 Poké (800 in the shop list).
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.19-21

name: Health Orb
outcome: Everyone in the blast has all status conditions healed. 300 Poké.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.19-21

name: Luminous Orb
outcome: Reveals the paths on the current floor, but not traps, treasure or hostile Pokémon. 300 Poké.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.19-21

name: Sunny Orb
outcome: Sunny Weather for a scene or until replaced. 300 Poké.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.19-21

name: Rainy Orb
outcome: Rain Weather for a scene or until replaced. 300 Poké.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.19-21

name: Sandstorm Orb
outcome: Sandstorm for a scene or until replaced. 300 Poké.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.19-21

name: Hail Orb
outcome: Hail for a scene or until replaced. 300 Poké.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.19-21

name: Observer Orb
outcome: Everyone in the blast stares at the lights, unable to move — as if all foes were Flinched. 300 Poké.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.19-21

name: All-Protect Orb
outcome: An energy barrier protects all teammates from the next three attacks that would damage them. 500 Poké.
source: PokéRole Mystery Dungeon Unofficial v2.0 (supplement) p.19-21

name: Guest party member

name: Adamant
roll: Confidence 4. Following your nature can restore Will.
outcome: An indomitable will that won't falter. Those with Adamant nature are belligerent and impassive. Only the strong survive in this world, that's why power and strength are what they respect the most. You are either their equal or you're inferior. Working as a team does not fit them well. They believe everyone must carry their own weight and those who can't will be left behind. They also lash out when they feel threatened and rarely care for social norms.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41

name: Bashful
roll: Confidence 6. Following your nature can restore Will.
outcome: There is an adorable shyness in them. They enjoy the simple things in life and are quite sensitive to other's emotions. They are very conscious about their own weaknesses and will try to make them better, but it hurts them to be pushed around and they may feel intimidated or disheartened if the challenges are too big. They need a strong figure who believes in them to feel confident but the fact that they are aware of their own weakness is a great advantage though.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41

name: Bold
roll: Confidence 9. Following your nature can restore Will.
outcome: Real thrill seekers. The Bold view life with optimism and excitement, they firmly believe one must go forward no matter the consequences. They are easily provoked and quick to take action, often heading into challenges a lot bigger than themselves. Failure is something that hits them hard, but they are known for getting back on their feet again and charge for adventure one more time. There's no mountain big enough to stop them and they love to be the center of attention.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41

name: Brave
roll: Confidence 9. Following your nature can restore Will.
outcome: The Brave of heart will face any situation with courage and a cool head. They won't tolerate bullying or abuse anywhere near them and will always encourage others to conquer their fears. “Selfless” is their second name, as they will never turn their back on their comrades even at the cost of their own safety. Others look up to them as they inspire confidence and trust. They strive to conquer their fears and wish to inspire others to do the same. They keep it together when stress begins to escalate.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41

name: Calm
roll: Confidence 8. Following your nature can restore Will.
outcome: Peace and tranquility is the most important thing for those with a Calm nature. They are not noisy nor they want many thrills in their lives. Conflict is not welcome and they tend to be peacemakers. It is rare to see them fall for provocations as they keep their distance and composure when facing trouble. They dislike stress and overbearing attention, but their presence is pleasant and soothing.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41

name: Careful
roll: Confidence 5. Following your nature can restore Will.
outcome: Those with this nature will often ponder their options according to the level of risk. If the benefit is substantial but the risk is too great they will prefer an option less rewarding but also less risky. They may take some time to warm up to strangers and will always be alert to their surroundings. Keeping a situation under control is important for them, not being in control makes them anxious and stressed. If things get out of hand they might run away to fight another day.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41

name: Docile
roll: Confidence 7. Following your nature can restore Will.
outcome: Always with a courteous disposition, a Docile nature indicates that you put others before yourself. Those under this nature love to please and be of assistance to their companions and community. They're not big achievers and might lack initiative, but even if only one person appreciates their efforts they will feel accomplished. They make great teammates and will be the first to ask: “How may I be of service?”
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41

name: Gentle
roll: Confidence 10. Following your nature can restore Will.
outcome: A Gentle personality reflects on graceful conversations and pleasant social interactions. They enjoy doing things with care and refinement, and others come to them simply to revel in their sophisticated presence. They enjoy luxuries but can be quite demanding with their tastes. These natural socialites were born to be in the spotlight and they don't like to share it.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41

name: Hardy
roll: Confidence 9. Following your nature can restore Will.
outcome: Life has been tough, but they know how to face anything no matter how difficult. The word “disheartened” is not for them, they have a great tolerance for stress and frustration so they rarely get worked up. You'll rarely find them unprepared. They do their best to endure and overcome. Taking things lightly is difficult for them, but they are dependable. They'll help you get through the hardest of scenarios.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41

name: Hasty
roll: Confidence 7. Following your nature can restore Will.
outcome: Energetic, spontaneous and a little impulsive. They live in the moment and don't have time to mop about past losses or worry about future battles. They are eager to see what comes next, moving from one thing to another. They rarely stress out because they make their lives on the go and rarely sit to relax or meditate things through. There will always be something to do with them around, let them improvise.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41

name: Impish
roll: Confidence 7. Following your nature can restore Will.
outcome: Free spirits hungry for enjoyment and fun at the expense of others. They carry themselves with a light heart but you can also see a smug smirk on their faces. Playful, irreverent and agile of mind, they dislike routine and chores. They are the kind to circle around a problem as a head-on confrontation will stress them. They also want a little validation from others so they'll get attention as the pranksters of the group.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41

name: Jolly
roll: Confidence 10. Following your nature can restore Will.
outcome: They love to spread happiness around and will always have a smile to give you. They rarely feel gloomy and dislike when others do. They easily form close friendships as others enjoy their good mood and affable disposition. They know the power to move a mountain lies in an enthusiastic demeanor and positive thoughts; regardless of the hard times their cheerful smile will brighten your day.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41

name: Lax
roll: Confidence 8. Following your nature can restore Will.
outcome: Lax is an inconstant nature, those under it will do things whenever they feel like it.   Is not that they are lazy, they just don't see the need to waste energy on stuff that's not important for them yet. Since they don't care to fill anyone's expectations they rarely stress out about social norms, but they'll need a reason to keep motivated and an even better reason to be pro-active instead of indifferent.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41

name: Lonely
roll: Confidence 5. Following your nature can restore Will.
outcome: They like to keep their distance and do everything on their own. They often feel it's up to them and nobody else to get things done and will take the burden of a responsibility that should be shared. Interacting with others is like a chore for them but being isolate also makes them feel misunderstood. They are hard to get close to but they can be trusted to do their best even if there's no one to guide them.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41

name: Mild
roll: Confidence 8. Following your nature can restore Will.
outcome: 'Harmless' is the word that best describes a Mild nature. They are patient and calm with others, reliable and caring on every matter. Because of this, others seek their company as stability ground. They seek to understand others and have a natural talent to do it. They tend to keep their needs to themselves and sometimes stay in the background, but they are the ones to turn when you need someone to listen.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41

name: Modest
roll: Confidence 10. Following your nature can restore Will.
outcome: When you are aware of your potential you don't need others to praise you for it. A modest nature knows the reward is the constant improvement of their abilities, not the acknowledging of others. They won't show off nor will they feel diminished when others display better capabilities. They'll do their best always and the only one who may judge the right or wrong of their ways is themselves.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41

name: Naive
roll: Confidence 7. Following your nature can restore Will.
outcome: The world is full of wonder; there is always something new to discover and many others to befriend. A Naive nature is a curious and innocent nature, they easily trust others because they ignore the many dan- gers of the world. They still have a lot to learn but they take life as it comes. They rarely stress out due to the fact they still don't know there are many things to stress about. A friend's smile and a hand to take it's all they need.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41

name: Naughty
roll: Confidence 6. Following your nature can restore Will.
outcome: Why should they listen to you? You are not their boss! Most of the time they'll deliberately do the opposite from what's expected from them. Why? Because they can, of course. They love to see others get mad and will use their clever mind and cunning to get away with their misdeeds. When they stress they put a cool facade, don't let that fool you. They need to be coaxed or put in their place to behave properly.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41

name: Quiet
roll: Confidence 5. Following your nature can restore Will.
outcome: Life is what happens around those with a Quiet nature. They often take a passive stance over the circumstances around them. Strong thoughts or opinions they have will rarely be expressed, so they are not the greatest at social interactions. They may be afraid to make a mistake or consider it a hassle to take action. When they manage to get the attention of others they rarely know what to do with themselves.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41

name: Quirky
roll: Confidence 9. Following your nature can restore Will.
outcome: You can't really understand how their mind works. Those who have a Quirky nature will usually see the world in a unique way that only they seem to comprehend. The way they act will be peculiar and often attract puzzled looks, they know they are oddballs and are fine with it, but they might get stressed by the strangest of things. The way they see the world is so unique that they accept new things easily.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41

name: Rash
roll: Confidence 6. Following your nature can restore Will.
outcome: They are reckless, and exposing themselves to danger is their idea of fun. Blunt and direct in the way they act with others, you are either their friend or you are their enemy. They are known for rushing into action with a “hit first, ask later” mentality. They are also famous for their quick-temper, loud-mouth, and foolhardy deeds, so don't expect them to keep their cool when stress starts to elevate.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41

name: Relaxed
roll: Confidence 8. Following your nature can restore Will.
outcome: The problems of the world are not their problems. A Relaxed nature will allow its bearer to take it easy and never lose their cool. They will never stress over trivial matters and won't instigate trouble. Should disputes arise, they will invite others to calm down through breathing and meditation, they go with the flow, never against it. Some may call them carefree, they will call themselves enlightened.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41

name: Sassy
roll: Confidence 7. Following your nature can restore Will.
outcome: They have an attitude, and those who take themselves too seriously may dislike it, but the Sassy natured are simply not afraid to voice their honest opinion and will always find ways to speak their mind and it's always brutally honest, so be ready for some burns. There are no middle grounds with them, they either love or hate something so they can be infuriatingly difficult or surprisingly easy to deal with, that is part of their charm.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41

name: Serious
roll: Confidence 4. Following your nature can restore Will.
outcome: They have a big sense of responsibility and won't appreciate when others don't take things seriously. Stress is a constant in their lives, if they have a duty to fulfill they will not stop until it's finished, everything else is a useless distraction once they have a task. They might need a hand since have a hard time relaxing but if you want things done well they are the ones to look for.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41

name: Timid
roll: Confidence 4. Following your nature can restore Will.
outcome: They have built walls around themselves that make it hard for others to see what's inside. They just want to be accepted but tend to worry too much and be way too harsh on themselves. Their confidence is usually placed on a leader figure and this makes them eager to please but also terrified to fail. They need to learn to trust in their own capabilities to reach their full potential.
source: PokéRole 2.0 Core Rulebook p.38-41
